issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff only adds a CPU-time check (time.process_time against HOP_START * TIME_FRACTION * time_limit). Once a best solution exists, it stops working through the pooled starts early. It reads no files, pastes no coordinates and uses no labels.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The check runs only after a solution exists, so solve still returns one. Validity is still checked exactly by the harness. This assumes HOP_START is defined elsewhere in the incumbent, since it is not in this diff. If it were missing, the job would crash rather than give a bad score.

Recomputed z: improvement = 2.9375 - 2.9370 = 0.0005. With sd 0.0034 per job, 1 candidate run and 2 incumbent runs, SE = 0.0034*sqrt(1 + 1/2) ≈ 0.00416, so z ≈ 0.12. That matches the harness's 0.125 within the rounding of the 4-decimal values. The gain is far inside the noise, so reject is the right decision.

The candidate has only 1 run. Its mean of 2.9375 is slightly above the best published value (~2.9370). Most likely this is noise or a lucky draw, not something wrong, because the harness checks validity exactly. Still, it is worth a replicate before reading anything into it.
